title: Grabovica and Uzdol: ARBiH Atrocities During Operation Neretva 93
sources: ICTY Halilovic Trial Judgment (IT-01-48-T, 16 November 2005), Grabovica/Uzdol crime findings and superior-responsibility acquittal
ICTY Halilovic Appeal Judgment (IT-01-48-A, 16 October 2007), prosecution appeal dismissed and acquittal affirmed
Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II, pp. 434-435, September 1993 fighting east of Prozor and along the Neretva
source_note: The Halilovic Trial Judgment establishes the crime findings at Grabovica and Uzdol while separately acquitting Sefer Halilovic because his superior authority and effective control over the perpetrators were not proved beyond reasonable doubt; the Appeal Judgment affirmed that outcome. Balkan Battlegrounds anchors the September 1993 operational chronology and Uzdol date. This informational essay adds no player choice, reward, collective-guilt claim, or copied source prose.
content:
During ARBiH operations in Herzegovina in September 1993, ARBiH soldiers killed Croat civilians at Grabovica and Uzdol. The ICTY prosecuted Sefer Halilovic on superior-responsibility charges connected to those crimes. The case produced two distinct findings that must remain separate: the Trial Chamber found that the killings were crimes, but it acquitted Halilovic of individual criminal responsibility.

At Grabovica on 8-9 September 1993, the Trial Chamber found beyond reasonable doubt that ARBiH soldiers killed at least 13 Croat civilians. The victims were inhabitants of the village, where ARBiH personnel had been accommodated during the operation. The finding attributes the killings to ARBiH personnel without assigning criminal responsibility to a commander whom the evidence did not place in effective control of the perpetrators.

At Uzdol on 14 September 1993, the Trial Chamber found that ARBiH personnel killed 29 civilians and one captured HVO soldier. Balkan Battlegrounds independently places the Uzdol fighting within the ARBiH offensive east of Prozor on that date. The tribunal record treats the killing of the civilians and prisoner of war as crimes committed during the operation.

The prosecution alleged that Halilovic had authority over the units involved and failed to prevent or punish the crimes. The Trial Chamber acquitted him because the prosecution did not prove beyond reasonable doubt that he was the superior of the perpetrators or exercised the effective control required for superior responsibility. The acquittal determined Halilovic's individual liability; it did not reverse the Chamber's findings that the Grabovica and Uzdol killings occurred and were crimes.

The Prosecution appealed. On 16 October 2007, the ICTY Appeal Chamber dismissed the appeal and affirmed the acquittal. The completed record therefore preserves accountability without substitution: ARBiH personnel committed the crimes found at Grabovica and Uzdol, while the evidence did not establish Halilovic's superior responsibility for those perpetrators.
